abstract: The germline gene set encoding the adaptive immune receptor repertoire (gAIRR) defines the allele space from which the expressed repertoire (exprAIRR) is assembled, so an incomplete gAIRR reference propagates errors into T cell receptor (TR) annotation and genotyping and is also a barrier to studying inherited TR variation in its own right. Human TR gAIRR diversity remains incompletely characterized because the loci resist short-read resolution and because locus-resolved cohorts have been small. We developed gAIRR Suite version 2, in which each gAIRR-annotate query carries 50 bp of germline sequence on either side of the allele core and a call is reported only when the assembly supports the core together with both flanks, and in which gAIRR-call genotypes from Element AVITI libraries whose 500-bp Read 1 spans a complete V core with its flanking anchors. Applying this framework to Human Pangenome Reference Consortium Release 2 (464 haplotype-resolved assemblies from 232 individuals across five superpopulations), we identified 531 novel TR alleles (486 TRV, 45 TRJ), each observed in the targeted-sequencing reads of at least one carrier, of which 298 were absent from our 47-individual Release 1 catalogue. In 216 individuals, targeted genotyping with gAIRR-seq and gAIRR-call recovered 99.985% of the 61,628 evaluated alleles found in the corresponding assemblies, with a precision of 99.995%. Release 2 added few common alleles but many rare ones: 407 of the 531 were restricted to a single superpopulation, and African-ancestry individuals accounted for 51.1% of these (46.0% {+/-} 2.1% after downsampling to equal group size) while comprising 30.2% of the cohort. Population-scale pangenome analysis therefore extends the TR gAIRR reference chiefly by recovering variation that smaller or less diverse cohorts would miss.
